assessment.headline: DAY 33 — WEEK 5. Markets rally on hope. Iran prepares for 6 months. The two narratives cannot coexist for long.
assessment.body:
Two completely contradictory narratives are running simultaneously. The MARKET narrative: Trump says 2-3 weeks, WSJ says he'll accept Hormuz staying closed, Sensex surges +1,870, VIX crashes 15%, Brent eases to $105. The IRAN narrative: FM Araghchi says 6+ months, hasn't responded to the 15-point plan, calls demands 'unrealistic,' IRGC threatening tech companies TODAY, parliament just approved permanent Hormuz tolls.

One of these narratives is wrong. The market will discover which one within the next 5 days (April 6 deadline).

CRITICAL ANALYTICAL REASSESSMENT (Week 5):

If deal by mid-April (30% probability):
• Brent drops to $85. Sensex rallies to 78,000+. Rupee recovers to ~92.5
• But Hormuz STAYS tolled — Iran's permanent revenue stream
• India's energy costs permanently higher by 5-10%

If war extends to May (45% probability):
• Brent $130+. Sensex could fall to 65,000. Rupee 98+
• LPG rationing tightens. CNG vehicles grounded. Fertilizer crisis hits Kharif crop
• FII outflow could reach $18B. RBI forced to raise rates despite slowdown

If war extends to June+ (25% probability):
• Brent $150+. Sensex below 60,000. Rupee past 100
• Full-blown stagflation. Food inflation double digits. Social unrest
• India forced to invoke bilateral agreements with Russia for crude
• Strategic petroleum reserves exhausted. Rationing of all petroleum products

For India today:
• Sensex 73,660 (+1,870 rally). Nifty 22,825. VIX -15%
• BW Elm reaches Mangalore today. 8 carriers crossed. 18 remain
• But FY26 ended worst since FY20. March was worst month in 6 years
• FII $12.3B outflow — record. Rupee 94.84 ATL. Indian basket $125/bbl
• The rally is real but the structural crisis hasn't changed

The most consequential fact today: Iran's parliament approved permanent Hormuz tolls. This means even in the BEST case scenario, India's energy import costs rise permanently. The pre-war world is gone.
